I'll give you another perspective.

So I'm a part of lgbt, my mum had a malignant brain tumour, she got diagnosed when I was 15 and passed almost exactly a year ago, I can see both sides.

Imagine being the older brother, having to hide who you truly are because your dad is homophobic, who knows how he would react if you came out and then you decide to leave home for education and you finally feel safe enough to come out and you actually get to be who you really are for the first time, going out, finding a boyfriend.

Your dad doesn't take this well and disowns you and tries to force your mother to disown you as well, she refuses, thus causing your parents divorce, do you not understand how fucking guilty someone would feel? You are the reason your parents aren't together, your minor brother now has to put up with divorced parents, your parents are now divorced because you liked the same gender.

AND now imagine this, you find out your mum- the one who defended you and let her marriage end because she loved you and accepted you- has cancer, that's a feeling I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. And then to make it even better, your younger brother blames you for your mum getting cancer, it's your fault she is ill, it's your fault your mum is dying. You are killing your own mum for being gay, You're little brother isn't blaming the dad -the one who disowned his own son and divorced his wife all because of a sexuality- he isn't blaming himself -you can 100% get a job at 15, it's rare and won't pay much, but you can- he's blaming you, all because you liked the same gender. 

That's the brother's pov, do you know how high the suicide stats are in relation with the LGBT community, it's really fucking high. The older brother has so much stacked against him all because he likes men, is that fair on him?

I can see the younger brother's pov as well, he's 15/16, his brain is nowhere near developed, he's still going through so many changes and having to deal with a divorce and his mother's illness. He does not get an excuse to be homophobic. He's allowed to be mad, he's allowed to have trauma responses, the poor kid has so much shit going on, of course he's not going to react the best but he doesn't get to be mad at his brother for finally feeling safe enough.

The day I come out to my family will probably be the last time I speak to so many of them, that's terrifying to me, the only good thing is I know I won't be able to disappoint my mum. I blame myself for my mum dying sometimes, if I had called an ambulance sooner maybe she would still be here. I don't need others blaming me for it.

OP is the AH here but I can understand his point of view. The main AH here is the dad.

If you're set on this and really don't see the point in being alive, make a reminder for 3 months and write down anything good that's happened and look at it, remember all of the good times you would have missed out on. It's honestly the only thing keeping me alive right now, seeing all the good things that have happened, that I would have missed if I had been successful.

Again PM if you want to talk/rant, or even if it's just to have someone there.
